problem: LLM-based robot control puts the LLM inside the perception-action loop, so it is slow (seconds) and often open-loop, which is unusable for reactive multi-robot navigation. Prior multi-robot LLM work is mostly simulated and text-token based.
motivation: Multi-robot teams need fast closed-loop control to react to each other, yet natural language is the most intuitive way to command them. Using a pretrained sentence-embedding LLM only once per task, and learning the policy offline from cheap real data, could give low-latency language-conditioned control with no simulator.
key_idea: Condition per-agent Q-policies on frozen sentence-embedding LLM vectors (computed once per task) and train them offline from combinatorially recombined single-robot random real-world data using an Expected SARSA (Mean/Soft Q) objective.
insight: Generalization to unseen commands comes from the LLM latent space: a decoder generalizes only for some LLMs (GTE-Base gives ~7 cm error on unseen tasks, while MiniLM gives ~1 m). Strong regularization toward the behavior policy (Mean Q / Soft Q) beats Max Q and CQL; Max Q overextrapolates around 15k epochs, and CQL/Max Q policies in the real world just hug the boundaries without reaching goals. Performance barely drops down to ~22 min of data, since 396 tasks and combinatorial multi-agent recombination multiply the training signal.
method: Task embedding: encode each natural-language command with a frozen GTE-Base feature-extraction LLM (768-d) once per task, keeping the LLM outside the control loop (<2 ms latency)

Combinatorial multi-agent augmentation: sample single-robot random-action transitions (5400 tuples, 90 min) and tasks independently and combine them on the fly into multi-agent transitions (~10^30 configurations)
Task-conditioned reward/termination: reward for progress toward the goal scaled by (1+v'+v), with a collision penalty, and termination on collision or leaving the arena
Expected SARSA objective: a one-line change to Q-learning replacing the max with the mean (Mean Q) or a softmax-weighted average (Soft Q), which stabilizes offline training

GNN architecture: fully-connected graph over agents where pairwise blocks (Linear+LayerNorm+LeakyReLU) over (o_i,z_i,o_j,z_j) produce a task-conditioned state s_i; dueling Q head, clipped double Q, IQL-style independent Q per agent
Learned simulator for analysis: a neural single-agent transition model applied per agent, used to compare objectives and data amounts
Deployment: a Boltzmann policy (τ=0.01) commands fixed-frame velocity targets at 1 Hz on real robots with no finetuning

setting.backbone: GTE-Base (frozen, task embeddings) + GNN Q-network trained from scratch with offline RL (Mean Q / Soft Q)
setting.model_size: GTE-Base ~110M (not stated in paper); Q-network hidden size 1024
setting.training_data: 5400 random-action transitions (90 min, 1 Hz) from a single real DJI RoboMaster; 396 train task phrasings, 8 unseen test tasks; multi-agent data synthesized by recombination; as little as 4-22 min suffices
setting.observation: 2D position and velocity of all agents (motion capture) plus each agent's language task embedding
setting.action_space: 9 discrete fixed-frame velocity actions (8 directions at 0.3 m/s + stop), 1 Hz
setting.simulator: real world only (plus a learned neural transition model for analysis)
setting.privileged: motion-capture positions/velocities of all robots; goal coordinates used only in the reward at training time

numbers.extra: unseen commands; success = mean distance to goal region < 25 cm; 30 s per task

numbers_note: Custom real-robot benchmark, not a standard navigation benchmark. Simulation results (distance, collisions) are given only in figures. Success counts are given in a caption.
results: Soft Q and Mean Q policies trained on ~20-90 min of random real data solve 8-9/10 unseen-command tasks with 3 robots and 18/20 with 5 robots, with near-zero collisions and <2 ms latency (1.51 ms for 5 agents). CQL and Max Q fail to reach goals in both simulation and real-world tests.
limitations: Restricted to simple 2D navigation to corners/edges with factorable per-agent rewards, discrete actions and a small template-based command set
Relies on motion capture for state; random-action data collection may not scale to larger state spaces; evaluation is small-scale (10-20 trials) with no external baselines
